findings.message: Hidden information: a grapple telegraph (GrappleSchema, apps/server/src/MatchRoom.ts updateViews/mirrorEncounters) goes into the view of anyone who sees the attacker, and it always carries defenderId (the target's session id). Grapple range is 6 tiles and sight radius is 10, so an observer who sees the attacker at the edge of sight learns the id, and from the aim and range the rough position, of a target outside its own sight radius. Observers only need the attacker and the aim to draw the telegraph. Blank defenderId for viewers who are neither the target nor able to see it. The worker recorded this as an open assumption, not a requirement.
findings.requirement: a client receives another player's attempt telegraphs, duel markers and ships only within its sight radius, through the existing `StateView` path.

findings.message: Integration check timing: the candidate run of `npm run test:integration` took 201 s (vitest Duration 201.10s; test files run one after another) of its 300 s check timeout. seaDuel.test.ts (31 s) and seaDuelHarness.test.ts (27 s) add about 58 s. A one-third margin on a shared machine is thin for 'well inside'. Consider running the sea-duel files in parallel with the rest, or trimming the 10 s absence and ready-timeout waits.
findings.requirement: The integration suite stays well inside its 300 s check timeout (split the harness if needed).

findings.message: The sea-duel browser scenario (tests/e2e/seaDuel.spec.ts) wins by tapping U with keyboard.press every 500 ms, up to 60 times. That does not hold attack keys, which is what the acceptance names. The KO and both players' result are still asserted, so this is a gap in how faithfully the test follows the spec, not a behaviour defect.
findings.requirement: the host wins with held attack keys, or the guest quits (choose one and assert it);

findings.message: Possible performance regression at sea: the arena of a sea duel runs inside the match page's Phaser.AUTO game (MatchGame in apps/web/src/seaScene.ts), which uses WebGL where available. The standalone arena deliberately uses the canvas renderer so that a machine without a GPU keeps its main thread free for the 4 ms DuelClient tick (docs/architecture.md 'Rendering'). On software-rendered WebGL a sea duel may starve that tick, which is not tested. The 'Rendering' paragraph in architecture.md now only holds for the standalone duel page.
findings.requirement: One Phaser game per page. The sea and the arena are scenes of that game. A duel never creates a second game.

findings.message: The sea scene's drawing of the duel marker (crossed swords and elapsed time) has no test. seaScene.ts publishes data-markers with position and elapsed text, but no unit or e2e test reads it; sea-duel has no third browser. Coverage stops at state delivery (tests/integration/seaDuel.test.ts watcher: marker at the encounter tile, stranger sees none) and the pure elapsedText formatter (apps/web/src/seaDuel.test.ts). The rendering, and whether it uses the marker's position and startTick, could regress unnoticed.
findings.requirement: a duel marker (crossed swords and elapsed time) shows at the encounter position to players in sight

findings.message: 'They stop' is not tested at room level. Every integration grapple that lands (seaDuel.test.ts first test, pairInRange/playersAt) places both ships at rest, so speed 0 and an unchanged position during the reservation would hold even if MatchRoom never stopped a moving ship. Only the pure stopShip helper is tested on a moving ship (simulation.test.ts). The e2e host coasts into the grapple but nothing asserts that its ship stops.
findings.requirement: a hit reserves both ships (they stop and ignore sailing input)

findings.message: The both-not-ready cancel test (seaDuel.test.ts 'cancels the duel when neither fighter is ready in time') asserts only the result ('cancelled', draw protection), not when it happens. The forfeit case checks >= 9.5 s since the grapple. A cancel at the countdown's end instead of 10 s would still pass.
findings.requirement: One client not ready at 10 s forfeits; both not ready cancels.

findings.message: The candidate's integration check took 201.1 s against its 300 s timeout (log-3: 'Duration 201.10s'). That leaves about a third of the budget on a shared machine. The harness was split into seaDuelHarness.test.ts, but the standalone duel.test.ts alone takes 69 s and files largely run in sequence.
findings.requirement: The integration suite stays well inside its 300 s check timeout (split the harness if needed).
